newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK bourse says 20-30 company listings in process.
newsitem.headline: HK bourse says 20-30 company listings in process.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong's listing department was handling 20 to 30 applications from companies seeking to list shares at the start of 1996, said Herbert Hui, deputy chief executive and head of listing.
"There are more than 20 to about 30 companies in process," Hui told reporters on Friday after a directors' conference held by the exchange.

"We have five teams and all them have been fully utilitised with several applications on hand," he said, adding he was not sure whether all the companies would be successful in getting a listing on the exchange.
A total of 49 companies were listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong in 1996, compared with 26 companies in 1995.
Hui also said that among the applicants were four to five Chinese state-owned enterprises seeking to list "H shares", a category reserved for such companies.
In December, China approved a fourth batch of 38 firms approved for listing shares overseas, with most of them expected to be listed on the Hong Kong stock market.
There are about 12 Chinese firms from earlier batches that have yet to obtain a listing.
